# wef-notch 0.6.0
**Every item within reach.** When the To-do list holds more than the card shows, click **+N more** to turn to the next page; the last page has **‹ Back** to the first. The card is back on its first page each time the Panel opens.
**Edit an item in place.** Double-click an item's text to change it: the text turns into a field, all of it selected. Return saves, Escape keeps what was there, and a click anywhere else saves too. To tick an item, click its circle; a click on the text alone does nothing, so nothing moves under a double-click.
**When you added it.** On the To-do tab each item shows when it was added, like `10 Nov 14:30`, beside its ×. Items added before this version show no time.
**A full list says so.** At 20 items the field reads **List full (20)** and Add dims, instead of quietly doing nothing.
**Installing for the first time?** Drag `wef-notch.app` into Applications with the Finder before you open it. Opened from Downloads first, macOS runs it from a hidden copy: it can't launch at login or update. The README's *Build and install* says how to put that right.

# wef-notch 0.5.0
**A Theme of your own.** Settings' Theme card has a seventh swatch, **Custom**, in a new third row beside two fields, **Body** and **Card**. Type or paste a colour as hex — `#22324A`, `22324a`, either works — and the Panel switches to it as the last digit lands. Everything else follows from your two colours: the words turn light or dark by whichever reads better against both. A half-typed colour changes nothing, and Escape or a click outside ends editing.
Custom starts in navy, a look none of the other six has. Your colours stay while you wear another Theme, so switching back brings them back.
**Installing for the first time?** Drag `wef-notch.app` into Applications with the Finder before you open it. Opened from Downloads first, macOS runs it from a hidden copy: it can't launch at login or update. The README's *Build and install* says how to put that right.

# wef-notch 0.4.0
**The rest of the week on the Today tab.** Once today's meetings are over, the tab's meetings half shows what's left of the week — tomorrow through the last day of your week, as your Mac counts it — each row with its day before the time (`Thu 10:00`, `Fri All day`). Up to six rows, then `+N more`; a click opens Calendar. Home, the bar and the meeting alerts still show today only.
On the week's last evening, `Nothing left today` sits in whichever half has nothing left.
**Installing for the first time?** Drag `wef-notch.app` into Applications with the Finder before you open it. Opened from Downloads first, macOS runs it from a hidden copy: it can't launch at login or update. The README's *Build and install* says how to put that right.
